# Sundhedsstyrelsen

Sundhedsstyrelsen (the Danish Health Authority) appears in the corpus as the regulatory body that approved [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK), the national clinical quality database tracking atrial fibrillation care in Denmark [^src1] [^src2]. This approval carries significant regulatory weight: once AFDK is implemented, Sundhedsstyrelsen's endorsement makes it legally mandatory ("lovpligtigt") for all hospitals, and eventually general medical practices, to report data into the database [^src1] [^src2].

The authority's role is mentioned identically across two editions of the AFDK annual report — the 2022–2023 report and the 2023–2024 report — underscoring that this approval is a stable, ongoing feature of AFDK's institutional foundation rather than a one-off event [^src1] [^src2]. Within the broader narrative of the annual reports, this mention sits alongside descriptions of AFDK as a nationwide clinical quality database anchored in the Danish Cardiological Society (Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab), tasked with monitoring and improving the quality of atrial fibrillation treatment in Denmark [^src2]. Sundhedsstyrelsen's approval is thus presented as a key mechanism ensuring comprehensive, compulsory data reporting that underpins the database's reliability and national coverage.

No further biographical, organizational, or historical details about Sundhedsstyrelsen itself are provided in the corpus beyond its approval role and the regulatory consequence of that approval.
